overview: Clients keep a WebSocket to a chat server (sticky via L4 LB). A message is assigned a per-conversation sequence, written to Cassandra (partition = conversation_id, clustering = message_id) and published to a Redis channel per user; whichever server holds the recipient's socket delivers it. If the recipient is offline the message waits in storage and a push notification goes out.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative sizing: 1M concurrent users; 50K connections per gateway.
estimation.calculation: 1,000,000 / 50,000 = 20 gateway instances before redundancy and headroom.
estimation.result: At least 20 connection-capacity units; provision more for failover and measured fan-out.
estimation.implication: Connection count and message fan-out need separate capacity budgets; partition history by conversation.

accessPatterns: Read messages after a sequence cursor; dedup sends by client message_id.
constraints: Partition by conversation_id and time bucket; assign order within a conversation and acknowledge only after durable acceptance.
relationships: conversation_id links the message to Conversation; sequence orders history inside that conversation.

accessPatterns: Authorize a sender and list members for delivery.
constraints: Membership checks precede sends; sequence allocation must have a single authority or a partitioned durable log.
relationships: Message records are partitioned by conversation_id; membership authorizes send and history access.

apiDetails.purpose: Send and receive conversation events over one persistent connection.
apiDetails.rationale: Dedup by messageId; distinguish durable acceptance, recipient delivery and read receipts. Reconnect resumes from the last acknowledged sequence.

apiDetails.purpose: Fetch missed messages after reconnect or load older history.
apiDetails.rationale: Use cursor pagination over conversation sequence, never a global ordering requirement.

steps.title: Mobile app → L4 LB → Chat servers → Message Service → Cassandra
steps.explanation: Authorize membership, dedup client message_id, assign a conversation sequence and persist before ack.

steps.title: Message Service → Redis Pub/Sub → Chat servers
steps.explanation: Publish the committed message; the recipient gateway delivers it if its socket is connected.

steps.title: Mobile app → L4 LB → History API → Cassandra
steps.explanation: Read messages after the last acknowledged sequence. A missed pub/sub notification does not lose durable history.

steps.title: Message Service → Push Notifications → APNs / FCM
steps.explanation: For offline recipients, send a push hint to reconnect and sync.

failureCases.scenario: Recipient disconnects after the send is acknowledged
failureCases.handling: Retain the durable message and let reconnect fetch by sequence. Pub/sub alone cannot replay missed delivery; push notifications only prompt a client to sync.

alternatives: Use write-before-publish pub/sub for low delivery latency with durable history recovery. Use Kafka fan-out when replay, independent consumers and burst buffering justify added latency and operating cost.
